target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: fix(signal): expose mention facts in inbound context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

## Summary

- Exposes Signal mention-gating facts on the generic inbound message context.
- Adds `CanDetectMention`, `HasAnyMention`, `EffectiveWasMentioned`, `MentionShouldSkip`, and `MentionSource` for delivered native/text mention decisions, while reusing the existing canonical `GroupRequireMention` field.
- Keeps the Signal mention source literal typed so SDK/context consumers can rely on `"native"` vs `"mention_pattern"`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. Skipped Signal turns still return before prompt/tool context is built, so this PR intentionally does not expose a public skipped-turn context field.

## Evidence

- Focused Signal/channel tests cover native mention facts being projected into inbound context:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `Mention*` parity with production inbound context.

  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`

### Operational Signal group evidence (2026-06-26)

target.title: fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal groups can be configured with `requireMention=true` so side chatter stays quiet until the bot is explicitly mentioned. Signal native mentions arrive as structured `dataMessage.mentions[]` metadata plus object-replacement characters in the message text. The current Signal handler renders those placeholders as `@<uuid>` or `@<phone>`, then relies on text mention regexes. Selecting the bot from Signal's native mention UI can therefore fail to wake the bot unless a matching text fallback happens to be configured.

This also leaves `canDetectMention` tied only to configured text regexes and passes `hasAnyMention=false` even when Signal supplied structured mention metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch keeps the fix inside the Signal plugin and adds a small native mention fact resolver. It compares structured Signal mention metadata against the current bot account identity:

- UUID via `channels.signal.accountUuid`
- phone number via the existing E.164 normalizer and `channels.signal.account`

The event handler now combines text fallback and native metadata:

- `wasMentioned` is true for text fallback or a native mention that targets the current bot account.
- `canDetectMention` reflects text regexes or available bot account identity.
- `hasAnyMention` reflects valid structured Signal mention metadata so the shared mention-decision contract can distinguish command bypass from messages mentioning someone else.

Mentions of other participants do not trigger the bot. Missing bot identity does not become a false mention. Existing text fallback, group access checks, pending history, attachment restraint, control-command handling, direct messages, and `requireMention=false` behavior stay unchanged.

This supersedes #69413, which was closed without merge, by adding the missing capability facts, event-handler coverage, and docs.

## User Impact

Before:

> A user could select the bot from Signal's native mention UI in a `requireMention` group and get no response because the rendered `@uuid`/`@phone` text did not match the configured agent-name regex.

After:

> Native Signal mentions targeting the current bot account pass mention gating. Mentions of other participants remain silent and are kept only as bounded pending context. A later bot mention can include recent skipped group context and reply in the same group.

Docs now describe Signal native mention behavior, `accountUuid`, text mention fallback, and a mention-gated group configuration with bounded history.

### Behavior Change

Signal groups with `requireMention=true` that have a configured bot identity (`accountUuid`/`account`) but no text mention regexes previously fell through to pass-through handling. After this change they enforce mention gating via native Signal mention metadata. Group chatter that did not mention the bot but previously reached it may now be gated. This is intended and makes native-only `requireMention` groups behave as documented. Maintainers with such groups should expect stricter, correct gating after upgrade.

### Trust Model

`dataMessage.mentions[]` is sender-supplied. A group member could craft metadata naming the bot; the only effect is waking the bot, which any member can already do via a normal Signal mention. Native facts are still validated against a real object-replacement placeholder span, so malformed metadata does not become a bot mention.

### Native Identity Note

For full native mention coverage, configure `channels.signal.accountUuid` alongside `channels.signal.account`. Phone-only identity can still match phone-backed mention metadata, but UUID-only Signal mention metadata requires `accountUuid`.

## Evidence

- Base: `4ecb45b chore: update default check gate expectations`
- Head: `83ac15c979a4`
- Static whitespace check: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Focused Signal mention-gating tests passed on this branch:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

The focused Signal suite covers:

- native bot UUID mention without text mention patterns;
- native bot phone mention with E.164 normalization;
- native mention of another participant stays silent and records pending context;
- malformed matching metadata does not become a bot mention;
- no-detector behavior remains explicit;
- helper facts for bot mention, unrelated mention, malformed span, and missing bot identity.

### Redacted Live Signal Proof

This is the sanitized inspectable artifact from a live 3-person private Signal smoke. IDs, UUIDs, phone numbers, group IDs, raw message bodies, and private participant context are intentionally omitted.

```text
environment: live private Signal group
runtime: OpenClaw gateway with this PR's Signal mention patch installed
config.runtime: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
config.template: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
signal.probe: { configured: true, running: true, probeOk: true, probeStatus: 200 }
session.markerScan: { proofMarker: "96738", markerFileCount: 11, rawContentPrinted: false }

case: native bot mention from Signal UI
input: Signal native mention picker selected the bot display name; no text mention regex fallback was used
expected PR facts: { canDetectMention: true, hasAnyMention: true, wasMentioned: true, shouldSkip: false }
observed: bot account replied in the same group with the controlled proof marker

case: native non-bot participant mention from Signal UI
input: Signal native mention picker selected another group participant, not the bot
delivery: Signal message info showed delivery to both the bot account and the mentioned participant
expected PR facts: { canDetectMention: true, hasAnyMention: true, wasMentioned: false, shouldSkip: true }
observed: no bot reply was produced after the quiet window
```

target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

## Evidence

Current head: `2461ca921f5665e8ac8e91c540ba567342ba64ee`.

- Focused default-agent proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/storage-scan.default-agent.test.ts src/agents/command/session.resolve-session-key.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.test.ts src/config/sessions/paths.default-agent.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-surface.test.ts` — passed 4 Vitest shards / 41 tests.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- Formatting: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/command/session.resolve-session-key.test.ts src/agents/command/session.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts src/commands/setup.ts src/config/sessions/paths.ts src/config/sessions/paths.default-agent.test.ts src/secrets/auth-store-paths.ts src/secrets/storage-scan.ts src/secrets/storage-scan.default-agent.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-surface.test.ts src/security/audit.ts` — passed.
- Touched-file lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/command/session.resolve-session-key.test.ts src/agents/command/session.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts src/commands/setup.ts src/config/sessions/paths.ts src/config/sessions/paths.default-agent.test.ts src/secrets/auth-store-paths.ts src/secrets/storage-scan.ts src/secrets/storage-scan.default-agent.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-surface.test.ts src/security/audit.ts` — passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- GitHub check rollup for current head includes passing CI, CodeQL/security, OpenGrep, dependency/security-sensitive guards, and Real behavior proof checks.

Closes #90573.
Supersedes stale #17477 without adding the previously proposed config/env fallback surface.

target.title: fix(channels): normalize phone identities with stray plus signs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Phone-based channel identities could normalize to unusable values when copied input contained doubled or embedded `+` characters. Digit-free input could also become the truthy identity `+`, causing incorrect routing comparisons instead of a clean invalid-input result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `normalizeE164` helper now strips provider prefixes and formatting, keeps digits only, returns exactly one leading `+`, and returns an empty string when no digits remain.

The maintainer rewrite also closes sibling cases exposed by that shared invariant:

- iMessage keeps non-phone `auto:` handles instead of collapsing them.
- Signal falls back to UUID identity when a source number contains no digits and rejects digit-free allowlist entries.
- Signal operator account setup remains strict about embedded or duplicate plus signs.
- WhatsApp setup tests exercise the real shared normalizer instead of a policy-copying mock.

## User Impact

Equivalent phone identities compare canonically across shared channel routing even when copied input contains stray plus signs. Invalid digit-free identities fail closed, while valid non-phone iMessage handles and Signal UUID senders retain intended routing.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `d7743db9177e12ee35893136cfea68e38ea3a0ba`.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox run `run_2cb4c42e20e4` found the prefixed Signal setup regression after 96 focused assertions passed. The branch was repaired to preserve strict setup validation and gained a focused regression.
- Source-blind final-code runtime contract passed: noisy UK/US numbers canonicalized; digit-free input returned empty; `auto:Alice Smith` remained `auto:AliceSmith`; digit-free Signal phone identity fell back to UUID; prefixed allowlist input parsed; embedded-plus setup input was rejected.
- Exact-head hosted CI run `28760402973`: all required checks passed.
- Fresh exact-head autoreview: clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.96.
- Targeted `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Focused duplicate search found no competing open shared E.164, WhatsApp, iMessage, or Signal normalization fix.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: yes, malformed copied phone identities now canonicalize or fail closed.
- Config/environment/migration: no change.
- Security/auth/network/tool execution: no change.
- Highest risk: channel identity matching and operator input validation.
- Mitigation: one permissive shared normalizer, strict Signal setup boundary, sibling channel regressions.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted maintainer rewrite and review
- [x] Source-blind behavior proof
- [x] Fresh structured autoreview

target.title: fix(browser): persist managed Chrome cookies across restarts
target.body:
## Summary
- Preserve managed `openclaw` browser cookies across restarts by letting Chrome close gracefully through browser-level CDP `Browser.close` before falling back to signals.
- For new local macOS headless managed profiles, launch Chrome with `--use-mock-keychain` and mark the profile so future launches keep the same cookie encryption backend.
- Leave existing managed profiles on their existing keychain backend; the PR does not switch an established profile to mock keychain.
- Add focused browser lifecycle/profile tests.

## What Problem This Solves
Managed browser sessions can hold login cookies in Chrome's live CDP cookie store while the profile's SQLite cookie DB remains empty. When OpenClaw stops and relaunches the managed browser without a graceful Chrome close, those cookies can disappear, so users lose authenticated browser state even when reusing the same managed profile.

Issue #96704 has a live repro against current upstream `origin/main` showing a CDP-visible persistent cookie before restart, `0` rows in Chrome's cookie DB, and `0` cookies after relaunch with the same profile.

## Security / Product Shape
This final version does **not** store cookies in an OpenClaw plaintext sidecar. Cookie material stays in Chrome's profile storage.

For new local macOS headless managed profiles, the PR opts the isolated OpenClaw-owned profile into Chromium's mock keychain so headless Chrome can persist encrypted cookies without login-keychain prompts. That marker is stored in the managed profile's `Local State`.

For existing managed profiles created before this PR, the PR does not change the cookie encryption backend. The recovery path is: existing profiles keep their current backend and gain graceful `Browser.close` shutdown; sessions already lost by previous ungraceful restarts cannot be reconstructed and require signing in again.

## Evidence
- Before-fix live repro against upstream main: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96704#issuecomment-4848117522
- Exact-head proof was captured on `96e8fa6c6629d9f0d7950fd295de0bf894dbecf6` using isolated temp gateway/browser ports `19984`/`19995`, synthetic cookies only, temp state dirs under `/private/tmp`, and channel startup disabled.
- Branch refresh `4377e6203386a3536e4125e8449543ef2d45d4ec` rebased onto current `origin/main`, removed the release-owned `CHANGELOG.md` edit, and kept the browser files identical to the proven head (`git diff --name-status 96e8fa6c6629..4377e620338 -- browser files` is empty).

target.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds
target.body:
### Summary

Codex/OpenClaw `exec` cannot reach a private-LAN host from the Mac mini, while the same macOS user and host can reach it from GUI Terminal, Browser, and a one-shot `launchd` agent.

This presents as normal OS/network failures (`No route to host`, `curl: (7)`), which makes the operator debug the LAN even though the LAN path is healthy.

### Environment

- Host: macOS on Mac mini, OpenClaw gateway running as user `andy`
- Exec path: Codex app-server spawned by OpenClaw gateway
- Target host: `192.168.147.163` (`docker-arr`)
- Target services checked:
  - Lidarr: `http://192.168.147.163:8686/`
  - SSH: `docker-arr` / `192.168.147.163:22`

### Reproduction

From OpenClaw/Codex `exec` on the Mac mini:

```sh
curl -sS -I --connect-timeout 5 http://192.168.147.163:8686/
# curl: (7) Failed to connect to 192.168.147.163 port 8686 after ... Couldn't connect to server

ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 docker-arr hostname
# ssh: connect to host 192.168.147.163 port 22: No route to host
```

However, from GUI Terminal as the same user on the same Mac mini:

```sh
curl -I http://192.168.147.163:8686/
# HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# Server: Kestrel

ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 docker-arr hostname
# docker-arr
```

A one-shot `LaunchAgent` bootstrapped into the GUI user context also succeeds:

```sh
curl -I http://192.168.147.163:8686/
# HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# Server: Kestrel

ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 docker-arr hostname
# docker-arr
```

One confusing detail: `traceroute -n -m 2 -w 1 192.168.147.163` from `exec` received a one-hop reply from `192.168.147.163`, while TCP/SSH/curl still failed.

### Expected behavior

If `exec` is allowed to use host networking, it should match same-user GUI/LaunchAgent reachability.

If this traffic is intentionally blocked by an OpenClaw/Codex policy boundary, `exec` should return an explicit policy error instead of OS-looking network errors.

### Actual behavior

`exec` fails with network-looking errors while the same user and host can reach the target through GUI Terminal, Browser, and LaunchAgent contexts.

This led to unnecessary debugging of the switch/LAN/VPN path before discovering that the failure was specific to the OpenClaw/Codex `exec` process context.

### Related but distinct issues

- #76260 covers `exec` bypassing `web_fetch` SSRF blocking. This issue is the inverse failure mode: `exec` cannot reach a LAN target that the same user context can reach.
- #39604 covers adding an opt-in private-network setting for `web_fetch`.
- #38931 covers browser/private-network SSRF confirmation behavior.

This issue is specifically about the `exec` runtime mismatch and the misleading error surface.

### Security note

I am not arguing that private-LAN access should be enabled unconditionally. If the block is intended, the safer behavior would be a clear policy/approval error and consistent documentation, rather than a misleading `No route to host`.

target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===

 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.body:
Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===
Old: await response.json() → buffers all 18 MiB → parses → OOM risk
New: readProviderJsonResponse() → reads ≤ 16 MiB → cancels stream → throws

PASS: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads prevent OOM.
```

**Tests** (20 passed):

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Includes 2 new oversized response rejection tests that verify:
- Token responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, `release()` called
- Create-card responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, both `release()` calls made

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu API call returning an oversized response (requires Feishu app credentials).

## Risk

Low. The 16 MiB cap matches the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` convention. Feishu API responses are normally under 1 KB. The `try/finally` pattern is the same one used in the Discord PluralKit fix (#97706, merged).

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===
Old: await response.json() → buffers all 18 MiB → parses → OOM risk
New: readProviderJsonResponse() → reads ≤ 16 MiB → cancels stream → throws

PASS: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads prevent OOM.
```

**Tests** (20 passed):

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Includes 2 new oversized response rejection tests that verify:
- Token responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, `release()` called
- Create-card responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, both `release()` calls made

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu API call returning an oversized response (requires Feishu app credentials).

## Risk

Low. The 16 MiB cap matches the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` convention. Feishu API responses are normally under 1 KB. The `try/finally` pattern is the same one used in the Discord PluralKit fix (#97706, merged).

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:
  - `{"scenario":"long-session-reset","beforeSize":57300171,"afterSize":0,"elapsedMs":1.22}`
  - `{"scenario":"capped-blank-prefix-corrupt-header","rejected":true,"preserved":true,"elapsedMs":12.07}`

target.title: feat(tencent): add Tencent Hy3 provider (TokenHub and TokenPlan)
target.body:
Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

## Evidence

Current PR head: `5b757c92b3ac2fa3433e76bf49b04a2c82fd6f6e`.

- `pnpm check:docs` — passed: docs formatting, markdownlint, MDX, i18n glossary, link audit, and docs map check. Rerun after glossary cleanup at `bb3d31c`.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — first run found missing TokenPlan built-in overlay validation; fixed in `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts` with coverage in `src/config/config-misc.test.ts`; rerun clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1 OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=0 OPENCLAW_QA_REDACT_PUBLIC_METADATA=1 OPENCLAW_QA_TRANSPORT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=180000 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-reply --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-99076-message-tool-stranded-after-main-merge` — passed 1/1; verifies the previously failing QA Smoke scenario after merging latest `origin/main`.

Supplementary verification / Docker Crabbox — Tencent TokenHub doctor/config repair and model-selection consistency (additional verification targeting old-config upgrade and model selection consistency):

- Focused tests (worktree `.worktrees/pr-99076` on head `706ac8245be`):
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tencent/config-compat.test.ts src/plugins/setup-registry.tencent.test.ts extensions/tencent/index.test.ts` — passed 2 Vitest shards, 14 tests (4 config-compat + 1 setup-registry + 9 index). Covers all four repair scenarios plus setup-registry dispatch.

The key source was `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`.

Supplementary Tencent TokenHub `reasoning_effort` live API probe (Docker, secret-safe, 2026-07-04):

- Key source: `openclaw2` `~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env` `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` (length 51), fetched via SSH command substitution into a one-shot env var. Never printed, written to a file, or persisted. Docker runtime: `node:24-bookworm-slim` image `sha256:242549cd46785b480c832479a730f4f2a20865d61ea2e404fdb2a5c3d3b73ecf` (same base as `scripts/e2e/Dockerfile` `bare`). Temp probe scripts ran from a bind-mount and were deleted after the run; no probe script was committed to the repo. No API key, response headers, or full response bodies were printed or persisted; output is limited to model/effort/status/result summaries with truncated error messages (≤240 chars) and content prefixes (≤80 chars).
- Endpoint: `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1/chat/completions`; prompt: short user message; `max_tokens: 8` (acceptance probe) or `64` (reasoning-content probe); `stream: false`.

hy3 live reasoning_effort acceptance (model=`hy3`):

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3 | high | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 |
| hy3 | none | 200 | ok; no reasoning_content; reasoning_tokens=0 (reasoning disabled) |
| hy3 | low | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats low as high) |
| hy3 | medium | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats medium as high) |
| hy3 | minimal | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats minimal as high) |

- Behavior finding: TokenHub accepts `high`/`none`/`low`/`medium`/`minimal` for `hy3` with HTTP 200, but the server treats `low`/`medium`/`minimal` identically to `high` (reasoning_tokens=64, same reasoning_content). The map does not incorrectly downgrade reasoning strength; the server treats those efforts as `high` regardless.

hy3-preview live verification — blocked by gateway permission:

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3-preview | (bare, no effort field) | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | high | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | low | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | none | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | minimal | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | medium | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | no_think | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

- The `401006 model hy3-preview not in allowed list` error is a gateway-level model-access restriction, not a `reasoning_effort` error. `/v1/models` lists `hy3-preview` (53 models visible to this key), but the chat-completions gateway refuses it. Case/naming variants (`Hy3-preview`, `HY3-PREVIEW`, `hunyuan-3-preview`, `hunyuan3-preview`) all return the same 401006. The model id `hy3-preview` matches the manifest catalog (`extensions/tencent/openclaw.plugin.json`) and the openclaw2 OpenClaw CLI, which also rejects `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview` with "Model override ... is not allowed for agent main". This is a TokenHub account permission restriction on the `openclaw2` key, not an OpenClaw code issue. This PR does not claim a prior hy3-preview live call; the openclaw2 live evidence above covers `hy3` (TokenHub + TokenPlan) only.
- Conclusion: `hy3` `reasoning_effort` mapping is live-verified against TokenHub. `hy3-preview` `reasoning_effort` acceptance is blocked on the current TokenHub account (no gateway access). Fully verifying the preview catalog's `["none","low","high"]` efforts requires a TokenHub key with `hy3-preview` completions access. The `stream.ts` code path that defers `minimal`/`medium` to the shared model fallback (resolving to `low` via `src/agents/openai-reasoning-effort.ts:152,164`) is internally consistent with the `reasoning_effort` spec, but cannot be live-confirmed under the current credentials.

- The earlier `QA Smoke CI` failure was in `message-tool-stranded-final-reply` under Crabline Telegram local-provider proof, not Tencent provider code. This branch does not carry QA harness or Telegram changes.

- The later `check-docs` failure was related to this PR's docs changes: `docs/docs_map.md` was stale and the zh-CN glossary lacked the new Tencent labels. Both are fixed and `pnpm check:docs` passes locally.

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
